title: MCP over streamable HTTP in hunch serve: one dispatcher for REST and MCP, stateless JSON, web-standard transport so Hono stays unreachable
context: Managed agent runtimes reach tools through an MCP gateway over HTTP; `hunch serve` only spoke REST and `hunch mcp` only stdio, so a remote orchestrator had no way to add the state layer as a tool target without a wrapper. The nuryel_* tools already exist for stdio in src/mcp/server.ts, bound to one store with a trusted caller; the served product resolves the principal from a credential and hosts several partitions. The production dependency audit (tooling/production-dependency-audit.mjs) keeps the reviewed Hono advisory (GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9) unreachable from production imports, and the SDK's Node transport (`server/streamableHttp.js`) imports @hono/node-server.
decision: Add `POST /nuryel/v1/mcp` to `hunch serve` (src/serve/mcpHttp.ts) registering the seven nuryel_* tools on a per-request McpServer. Refactor src/serve/app.ts so the REST routes and the MCP tools call ONE `dispatch(route, principal, body, config)`; grants, the write lock, flushes and refusal mapping live there once. The endpoint is stateless (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`, `enableJsonResponse: true`; GET/DELETE are 405) because every verb is one request/response. Authentication is the existing bearer/DPoP block, run before the MCP handler; tool arguments are the request schemas minus `schema` and `principal`, and a smuggled principal is ignored. A refusal is a tool error (`isError: true`) whose structuredContent is the REST problem body, so both transports report the same 403/409/422/400. Use `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` and bridge IncomingMessage → Request → ServerResponse in ~15 lines (only accept, content-type and mcp-* headers travel; the body was already read and bounded by readBody), so the Hono-importing Node wrapper never enters production imports.
consequences: Two transports, one rule set: any new served verb is added to `dispatch` and appears on REST (POST_ROUTES) and MCP (TOOLS) by registration only.
Per-request McpServer construction costs a few tool registrations per call; acceptable for the escalation-path volume this serves, and stateless means no eviction logic.
Error handling after the MCP response is on the wire cannot send a problem body (headersSent guard ends the response).
Header bridging is an allowlist: an MCP client feature that depends on another header (e.g. future auth or origin checks) must be added to the list explicitly.
alternatives_rejected: Register the HTTP tools by reusing the stdio registrations in src/mcp/server.ts — those bind one store and take the principal from arguments (trusted caller); the served product must derive it from the credential and route to a partition per scope, so sharing the code would either leak the argument principal or fork the server file.

Session-ful MCP (session ids, GET event stream, DELETE) — no verb needs server-initiated messages; sessions add state to a server whose partitions are on disk and would need eviction and cross-process handling for nothing.

The SDK's Node `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` — imports @hono/node-server; the dependency audit fails closed on it (test/production-dependency-audit.test.ts) and the exception is reviewed byte-exact for a reason.
A separate port or process for MCP — the credential, grants, write lock and problem mapping would have to be duplicated; the whole point is one binding.
